summary: audio-accuracy (quality phase). I built a realistic piano benchmark, measured the shipped pipeline on it and improved it. On the main track, I compared it with a piano-specific model (Magenta.js Onsets and Frames) in a sandbox. (1) BENCHMARK: test/fixtures/real/ holds 12 files (3.1 MB of audio, 14-25 s each) with exact ground truth. They are rendered from the full Salamander Grand Piano V3 (Alexander Holm, CC BY 3.0, 16 velocity layers; the samples stay in my temp folder) with sustain pedal, sympathetic resonance, damper and pedal noise, rubato +-8 %, onset jitter, ritardando, dynamics and voicing. The pieces are a recreated piano-cover ballad (70 bpm, heavy pedal, melody in octaves 5-6, soft left-hand arpeggios above middle C, as the lead asked; original, CC0), Für Elise, Moonlight I, Mozart K.545, Gymnopédie 1 and Liszt Liebestraum No. 3 (pickup + bars 1-5, read from the typeset IMSLP edition #111552). Conditions: estudio (room, x4), sala (concert hall RT60 2.3 s: Liebestraum, Gymnopédie), desafinado (+40 cents; A=432 Hz = -32 cents), acelerado (TikTok speed-ups with pitch: Für Elise 1.15x = +2 semitones +42 cents in an mp4 with video; Liebestraum 1.10x = +2 st -35 c), movil (AAC video audio played on a phone speaker and re-recorded by a phone mic: ~380 Hz-7.5 kHz, distortion, room, noise, AGC, Opus; ballad, and Moonlight 1.25x). Each JSON has notes (pitch, start, key duration, sounding duration, velocity, hand, role melody/arpeggio/accompaniment/bass/inner), sustain-pedal spans, beat and downbeat times, key and meter. score-accuracy already uses them. (2) BASELINE (Basic Pitch as shipped, onset +-50 ms): mean F1 0.744 (estudio 0.905, sala 0.888, desafinado 0.467, acelerado 0.491, movil 0.811). Detuned and sped-up audio collapses: recall 17-51 %. The notes are not read a semitone off; they are simply not detected, because the energy splits between two semitone bins. This is very likely what the client heard as 'lee fatal'. Liebestraum arpeggio recall: 81 % in the hall, 4 % sped up. Soft notes: 60 %. Velocity correlation r = 0.01. Octave ghosts of soft bass and arpeggio notes are the main source of extra notes. (3) IMPROVEMENTS SHIPPED in the Basic Pitch worker: (a) global tuning estimation and compensation (src/engine/transcribe/tuning.ts). Spectral peaks go into a circular histogram of cents deviations. It is accurate to 2.5 cents on every benchmark file, codec and phone chain included, and takes 10-60 ms per 20 s. When the offset is >= 8 cents and confidence >= 0.35, the input is resampled with a Kaiser-windowed sinc and note times are scaled back. (b) Loudness velocities from the audio (src/engine/transcribe/velocity.ts): partial energy gained right after each onset, minus what was already ringing under the pedal, in dB relative to the piece, mapped to 0.15-1. The scale is fitted on the benchmark (velocity MAE 0.31 -> 0.15). AFTER (shipped): mean F1 0.873 (estudio 0.905, sala 0.888, desafinado 0.870, acelerado 0.880, movil 0.791). Liebestraum arpeggio recall 81 % / 74 % (sped up, was 4 %), soft-note recall 79 %, velocity r 0.47, onset MAE 5.7 ms, bias -1.6 ms. The legacy fixtures are unchanged (synthetic 0.971, FluidR3 piano 0.869, all 0.920; scale.wav 1.00; silence 0 notes). Lead's pedal points: soft pedalled accompaniment survives (velocity floor 0.15 > buildScore minVelocity 0.1; notes >= 93 ms > minDuration 50 ms). Pedal re-triggers are rare (7 extra notes, 8 merged repeats on the whole benchmark). Onsets stay tight under pedal. Not changed: decoder thresholds. A real-piano sweep prefers onset 0.75 / frame 0.35 (+0.015 F1) but loses 0.03 on the FluidR3 fixtures. (4) MODEL COMPARISON (sandbox only; @magenta/music 1.23.1 and the onsets_frames_uni checkpoint installed in my temp folder, nothing added to the project). Onsets and Frames clearly beats Basic Pitch on piano. Same benchmark, same metrics, both with the same tuning compensation: mean F1 0.940 vs 0.873. Per condition (OaF / Basic Pitch): estudio 0.965/0.905, sala 0.976/0.888, desafinado 0.946/0.870, acelerado 0.980/0.880, movil 0.805/0.791. Liebestraum arpeggio recall 94 % / 92 % (sped up) vs 81 % / 74 %. Soft notes 86 % vs 79 %. Velocity r 0.75 (dedicated velocity head) vs 0.47. Legacy FluidR3 piano fixtures: 0.974 vs 0.869. Without tuning compensation, OaF scores 0.904 (desafinado 0.832, acelerado 0.855), so the compensation helps both models. OaF is weaker on onset timing (32 ms frames: MAE 11 ms after a constant +15 ms shift, vs 5.7 ms), merges some re-strikes under pedal and gives octave errors on band-limited phone audio. Costs on this PC (RTX 2060, headless Chrome, 30 s of audio): OaF WebGL 3.6x real time (mel spectrogram in JS 4.8 s + model 3.5 s), Basic Pitch 18.6x. On the tfjs CPU backend (proxy for phones without a usable GPU): OaF 0.23x (128 s for 30 s), Basic Pitch 0.5x. Load + warm-up: OaF 8-18 s, Basic Pitch 7-10 s. Download: OaF checkpoint 62.5 MB float32. I quantized it in the sandbox: float16 29.8 MiB with identical F1 0.940; uint8 14.9 MiB with F1 0.937. Basic Pitch is 0.9 MB. Memory: OaF 60 MB of weights in tensors and ~390 MB GPU peak with 4 parallel batches. tfjs 3.21 (the project's version) runs the official OaF code unchanged and reproduces the tfjs 2.8.6 outputs exactly, apart from one tfjs 3.21 WebGL shader bug on uneven last chunks. Padding the mel frames to whole chunks fixes it (verified on all 12 files). LICENSES: Magenta.js code is Apache-2.0. The checkpoint page states no license (it asks high-traffic apps to mirror the files), and Magenta says its piano checkpoints are trained on MAESTRO, which is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (non-commercial, share-alike). Basic Pitch (Apache-2.0 code and model) was ALSO trained on MAESTRO (paper Table 1), so the open question of whether NC terms reach the weights applies equally to the model we already ship. Legal advice is needed before any commercial release, for either model. RECOMMENDATION (lead and client decide): adopt Onsets and Frames as the piano model (the client only transcribes solo piano), with tuning compensation, and keep Basic Pitch as the fallback for devices without WebGL or that are too slow. Integration plan in public_api_notes. Client feedback applied: 16:20 (realistic benchmark, before/after, tuning so accidentals and sharps come out right), 16:35 audio side (ballad texture benchmark; pitches), 16:45 (Liebestraum benchmark, arpeggio recall, piano-model comparison as the main track).

public_api_notes:
TRANSCRIBE: transcribe(samples, { sensitivity, minNoteMs }) is unchanged, and so are its defaults (0.5 / 90) and the progress stages. Tuning compensation is automatic inside the worker, and note times are always in seconds of the samples you pass. NoteEvent.velocity CHANGED MEANING: it used to be Basic Pitch's detection confidence (about 0.3-0.6 for every note, uncorrelated with loudness). It is now loudness relative to the piece: forte notes near 0.7, soft accompaniment around 0.3, floor 0.15, max 1. ScoreEvent.velocities (score-accuracy) and the new piano playback therefore get real dynamics. The default minVelocity 0.1 keeps every note, but the viewer's 'Ruido' filter now removes soft notes rather than doubtful ones (see requests). Existing library items keep their old velocities. New: type TuningInfo { cents, confidence, applied } (exported from src/engine/transcribe/index.ts) and TranscribeDetails.tuning, reached through the startTranscription test hook only. app code still imports nothing but index.ts. Bundle: the worker chunk grows 4.6 KiB (1779.6 KiB), and tfjs and basic-pitch stay out of every other chunk (check-bundle 4/4 PASS).
BENCHMARK: node scripts/fixtures/check-transcription.mjs runs the legacy fixtures plus the realistic benchmark. --real-only runs only the realistic one (about 1.5 min); --json <file> saves results for diffs; --tuning off|<cents> overrides the compensation; --sweep-real sweeps thresholds on cached activations; --dump <dir> writes raw activations and detected notes per fixture (useful for offline score tests). The default port is now 5197, falling back to the next free one. Ground-truth JSON (test/fixtures/real/<name>.json): name, title, composer, condition (estudio|sala|desafinado|acelerado|movil), file, description, source, sampleRate, duration, speed, detuneCents, transpose (semitones already applied to the pitches), residualCents, codecDelayMs (0: ffmpeg trims AAC priming, and Chrome does too, so onset bias is about 0), key {tonic, mode, fifths} (after transposition), timeSignature (+meterNote for Für Elise 3/8->3/4, Moonlight 2/2 and Liebestraum 6/4), beatsPerBar, pickupBeats, bpm (x speed), beats[] and downbeats[] (seconds, rubato included), pedal[{start,end}] (seconds), notes[{pitch, start, duration (key held), sounding (until damper or pedal lift, re-strike or natural decay), velocity 0..1, hand, role}]. Regenerate with: node scripts/fixtures/make-real-fixtures.mjs --samples <folder with SalamanderGrandPianoV3.sfz> [--only name,...]. It is deterministic and needs ffmpeg with aac, libopus and libx264.
ONSETS AND FRAMES INTEGRATION PLAN (only if the lead and the client approve it; nothing has been added): (1) Do not add @magenta/music: it pulls tfjs 2.x, tone, protobufjs and more. Vendor the roughly 300 lines needed instead (Apache-2.0, keep the attribution and add a NOTICE): mel front end, AcousticCnn + Lstm builder (tfjs Layers API, verified to run on our tfjs 3.21 with identical output), batching and the onset/frame decoder (thresholds 0.5; the sweep confirms 0.5). Put them in src/engine/transcribe/oaf/, imported only by the worker. (2) tfjs 3.21: pad the mel frames to whole 250-frame chunks and trim the outputs. This avoids a WebGL shader compile bug ('getT1 no matching overloaded function') that otherwise fails on some lengths. Use 1-2 parallel chunks instead of 4 to lower GPU memory for phones (~390 MB peak with 4). (3) Model files: ship the checkpoint quantized to uint8 (14.9 MiB, F1 -0.003) or float16 (29.8 MiB, identical). The manifest format is the standard tfjs weights manifest with a 'quantization' field, which loadWeights decodes. Store it in public/models/onsets-frames/ with its notice. Either precache it (raise Workbox maximumFileSizeToCacheInBytes above the 4 MB shard size) or download it lazily on first use with progress, and cache it in Cache Storage. (4) Speed: compute the mel spectrogram with tfjs on the GPU (tf.signal.stft + a precomputed mel matrix). The JS mel is 50-60 % of OaF's time, so expect about 2x. Report progress per chunk. (5) Pipeline: keep tuning.ts in front of the model (OaF desafinado 0.832 -> 0.946, acelerado 0.855 -> 0.980). Add +15 ms to onsets (constant bias of the 32 ms frames). Velocity = OaF velocity head (10..90) / 100. (6) Fallback: Basic Pitch when WebGL2 is missing, when OaF's warm-up fails, or when a short timing probe predicts more than about 1x real time. Optionally a setting 'Modelo: Preciso (piano) / Rápido'. (7) Tests: give check-transcription a model switch, so both stay measured on the same benchmark. (8) Resolve the MAESTRO non-commercial question first, for both models. Sandbox to reproduce: C:/Users/Marcos/AppData/Local/Temp/pauta/audio-accuracy/oaf-sandbox (run-oaf.mjs [--tfjs3 --pad --tuning --shift 15 --backend cpu --perf 30 --ckpt onsets_frames_uni_uint8 --sweep --official], quantize.mjs), results in ../results/*.json|txt.

requests.request: Decide on adopting Magenta.js Onsets and Frames as the piano model, with Basic Pitch as fallback. The numbers and integration plan are in this report (summary and public_api_notes): F1 0.940 vs 0.873 on the realistic benchmark; costs +15 MB (uint8) of model download and about 5x slower inference; licenses: Apache-2.0 code, weights trained on MAESTRO (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0), just like Basic Pitch's. Get legal advice on the non-commercial clause before any commercial release, for either model.

Commit the new untracked files of my area: scripts/fixtures/lib/, scripts/fixtures/make-real-fixtures.mjs, scripts/fixtures/real-pieces.mjs, src/engine/transcribe/tuning.ts + tuning.test.ts, velocity.ts + velocity.test.ts, test/harness/metrics.test.ts and test/fixtures/real/ (24 files, 3.3 MB). DEFAULT_SETTINGS needs no change: sensitivity 0.5 and minNoteMs 90 remain the calibrated defaults.

NoteEvent.velocity now means loudness (0.15-1; forte about 0.7, soft accompaniment about 0.3) instead of model confidence (about 0.3-0.6). The 'Ruido' slider (minVelocity 0-0.8) would now delete soft accompaniment from about 0.3 up. Consider capping it near 0.3, or relabelling it as a dynamics filter. The default 0.1 is safe.

For your information: realistic transcriptions for node tests can be dumped with node scripts/fixtures/check-transcription.mjs --real-only --dump <dir> (<fixture>.notes.json). Ground truth in test/fixtures/real/*.json has hand and role per note, pedal spans and beats (format in public_api_notes). Velocities are now loudness-based, so the 'merged notes keep the loudest' rule works as intended.

known_issues: Phone-speaker captures lose everything below about 380 Hz. Notes whose fundamental falls under that cutoff are read an octave up (for example C4 as C5), in both Basic Pitch and Onsets and Frames: phone-moonlight-125 has 16 and 24 octave extras. Applying the correct tuning (-13 cents) on that file also let more of these ghosts through (F1 0.78 -> 0.74), while every other file improved. Not fixed.

Octave ghosts (+12 above soft bass and arpeggio notes) remain Basic Pitch's main source of extra notes: 89 on the benchmark. A simple ratio filter would also delete the real octaves the benchmark contains (left-hand octaves, doubled melody), so none was added.
Re-strikes of a pitch that is still sounding under the pedal: Basic Pitch misses some (Moonlight's repeated G#3), and Onsets and Frames merges more (33 'merged' on the benchmark).

Velocities are relative within a piece, because the input is peak-normalized: a uniformly pianissimo piece comes out mezzo. No register correction (a global slope helped some pieces and hurt others). On phone captures without bass the velocities are unreliable (r 0.35); on Für Elise, with a narrow true dynamic range, r is 0.13.

Basic Pitch notes under the pedal end before the pedal lifts ('too short' versus the sounding duration), because the decay fades below threshold. The score's pedal marks (Score.pedals) carry the sustain. In dry Mozart, energy tolerance makes many notes about 100 ms too long (47 'too long'); lowering it did not change F1 and was left as is.
The benchmark is rendered: one sampled piano (Salamander), synthetic rooms and a simulated phone. Item (b), a qualitative check on a real CC0 recording (e.g. Kimiko Ishizaka's BWV 846), was not done.

Onsets and Frames on tfjs 3.21 needs the chunk-padding workaround (WebGL shader bug on uneven last chunks). Its 62 MB float32 checkpoint must be quantized for a reasonable PWA download. Phone performance was not measured (only the tfjs CPU backend on this PC: 0.23x real time).

IMSLP sits behind a JavaScript interstitial, so I did not script it (no bot-protection bypass). The Liebestraum score came from the public Internet Archive / Wikimedia Commons mirror of IMSLP #111552 and was read with PyMuPDF installed only in my temp folder.
